name: Baglioni Masseria Muzza
insider_take: This restored 16th-century masseria sits on 40 hectares of ancient olive groves in the heart of Salento, where centuries-old trulli structures meet contemporary luxury in Italy's hidden southern gem.
whats_special: The property features its own organic olive oil production from 4,000 olive trees, some over 500 years old. The masseria's original stone walls and vaulted ceilings house a world-class spa using local ingredients like olive oil and sea salt from nearby Otranto's pristine coastline.
pro_tip: Book a private olive oil tasting session during harvest season (October-November) to witness the ancient milling process and taste liquid gold straight from trees that predate Columbus.
dont_miss: The UNESCO World Heritage site of Alberobello is just 30 minutes away, home to over 1,500 iconic trulli houses. Also explore the baroque city of Lecce, known as the "Florence of the South," and the crystal-clear waters of Porto Cesareo Marine Protected Area.
pros: Historic 16th-century masseria with authentic Puglian architecture
Stunning countryside location surrounded by olive groves and Mediterranean gardens
Luxurious spa featuring traditional treatments and wellness experiences
Exceptional farm-to-table dining with local Puglian ingredients
cons: Remote countryside location requires car for exploring nearby towns
Limited evening entertainment options due to rural setting
